newsitem.title: FINLAND: OFFICIAL SEES NOTHING BOOSTING FINNISH 98 SPENDING.
newsitem.headline: OFFICIAL SEES NOTHING BOOSTING FINNISH 98 SPENDING.

text.p: The finance ministry's deputy budget chief Hannu Makinen said on Friday he saw no upward pressure on budget spending in 1998, which has earlier been agreed at 191 billion markka.

"There is nothing in sight that would up spending (in 1998)," he told Reuters by telephone, but added that the finance ministry's economists had not yet presented the forecasts that the budget will be built on.
The finance ministry will start talks on its budget proposal on Monday, and the government is due to decide on the budget on August 13-15.
The government decided in February that budget expenditure in 1998 and 1999 would be 191 billion markka and 192 billion markka respectively, down from some 196.5 billion this year.
It said in June the situation was mostly unchanged and that budget proposals would be in line with the February decision.
Finland has adopted an austere fiscal policy to curb a rise in state debt, and has said it aims to meet the criteria for joining Economic and Monetary Union among the first in 1999.
